newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian group sees big role in Russian gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian group sees big role in Russian gas deal.

text.p: Bulgaria's Multigroup conglomerate is well placed to profit from an agreement signed by the Bulgarian and Russian prime ministers for transiting Russian gas through Bulgaria to the Balkans.

The project will be operated by the Topenergy joint stock company, in which Russia's Gazprom has 50 percent and Bulgargas 25.1 percent. Multigroup has 8.5 percent directly and a half share of private firm Overgas's 8.5 percent stake, and is involved at the finance, construction and marketing levels.
"The project will establish the industrial base for the future of Bulgaria," Multigroup President Ilia Pavlov said.

The gas pipelines are vital to Russia's energy expansion plans as well as to the Bulgarian economy but the deal dragged on under the less market-oriented former Socialist government, which Pavlov said had failed to adapt to the new Western-style business environment in Russia.
"The Russians have changed their mentality," he told Reuters. "We were the first from this region to realise this because we were talking the same business language as them."
Investment of $560 million over three to five years will be followed after 2003 by annual transit tax revenue of $100 to $110 million.

Multigroup will finance part of the project together with Gazprom, and will participate in the tenders for building the infrastructure. It also stands to gain as a gas supplier from the expansion of the market the project entails.
Pavlov said the company was consolidating its other activities to concentrate on gas.
Multigroup traces its origins back to the communist-era Multiart cooperative founded in 1988 which was involved in project development and promotion activities.
Today, Multigroup employs more than 15,000 people and its commodities trading and financial operations activities produce an annual turnover of $1.5 billion.
Multigroup is one of a small number of businesses flourishing amid Bulgaria's economic chaos, and has sometimes attracted adverse publicity.
"We realise that we are something of a phenomenon by Bulgarian standards," said Pavlov, a former member of Bulgaria's national wrestling team.
Its commodities activities are mainly in oil and gas, non-ferrous metals, sugar, coffee, cocoa and other products.

Tourist sector investments account for 55 percent of Bulgaria's winter tourism and 50 percent of summer tourism, while in the investment banking field, it is active in asset trading and management in emerging markets instruments.
Multigroup has stakes in Bulgaria's Creditbank and a bank in Macedonia, and manages the Multigroupelit voucher privatisation fund.
The company is registered in Bulgaria and in Liechtenstein, and operates subsidiaries in Britain, the United States, Russia, Ukraine, Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
